blocks.text: What is a medical certificate for leave?

A medical certificate for leave is a short document from a doctor stating that you were assessed and found unfit for work or study for a set period, or fit to work only from home. The certificate supports a leave request to an employer, university or school.
The note records the dates and the doctor's opinion on your fitness. A leave certificate is not a treatment plan, a prescription or a legal report.

On the DrCertificate form, two options match this topic. Choose the Sick Leave option, listed for university or work, when you need time off. Choose the Work From Home option when you can work but should stay away from the office. A general medical certificate also uses the Sick Leave option.
People often mix up a sick leave note and a medical fitness certificate. A fitness certificate says you are fit for work, sport or travel, and uses the Medical Fitness Certificate option instead.
When do you need a medical certificate for leave?

items: You need a medical certificate for leave when an employer, university or school asks for proof that illness kept you away. HR teams, school offices and course coordinators are the people who usually request one.
At work, HR may ask for a note after a single sick day, or once you pass the number of days your company lets you self certify. Rules differ by company and by country.
Students face the same request. A university may want a note to excuse a missed class, a late assignment or an exam, and a school office may ask for one after a student misses days.

Work from home notes fit a different case. You feel able to work but should keep away from colleagues, for instance with a cough or a mild fever, and your manager wants a doctor's opinion before agreeing. If illness stops you from travelling, an airline or travel provider may ask for a note too, which uses the Unfit to Travel option on the form.

Why do organisations ask at all? Paid leave costs money. A doctor's note gives the employer or school a record that the absence had a medical reason, and it protects you if anyone questions the absence later.

blocks.text: Who issues a medical certificate for leave on DrCertificate?

Independent doctors issue every certificate on DrCertificate. Each doctor holds an MBBS, MD or MS qualification and is registered with a medical council, and the doctor alone decides whether a certificate is issued.

DrCertificate is an online platform run by Health Venture OU. The platform connects applicants with doctors through an online form and a digital chat. DrCertificate does not diagnose, treat or prescribe.

Why does the split matter? Your employer is relying on a medical opinion, so paying for a request buys a doctor's review and not a guaranteed note. Doctors decline about 2% of requests, for example when the name and ID do not match or when the symptoms and details shared are inconsistent.
Customers are encouraged to check that the place of submission accepts online medical notes before choosing the service.

What should a medical certificate for leave include?

A medical certificate for leave should show your full name, the dates it covers, its purpose and the issuing doctor's details. HR or a school office looks at those items first, so a missing one can hold up your leave.
Run through the checklist before you send the PDF.

Ask your HR team or school office about their own format first. A university might want the note uploaded to a student portal, and an employer might set a deadline for handing it in. A certificate cannot be corrected once issued unless the fault is from the medical team, so getting your details right on the form saves trouble.

items: Your name Matches your ID and your employer or school records.
The dates Cover the days you were away, with the right start date.
The purpose Says sick leave or work from home, whichever you asked for.
Doctor details Show who issued the certificate.

blocks.text: Will your employer or school accept a medical certificate online?
Your employer or school decides whether to accept a medical certificate online, not DrCertificate and not the doctor. Policies differ between companies and institutions, so ask before you apply.
Certificates get questioned for predictable reasons.

The most common is the wrong type of note, for example a fitness certificate sent when HR wanted a sick leave note. Wrong or missing details come next, like a name that does not match staff records. An organisation may also accept only notes from its own panel clinic or a local doctor, and a late submission can be refused even when the note is in order.

If HR or a school office questions your certificate, ask which detail or rule caused the problem. Share the doctor's details shown on the certificate if they want to confirm it. If the organisation accepts notes only from a named clinic, you will need to visit that clinic.
Payments are non refundable. Checking first saves you money.
When is an online medical certificate for leave not the right choice?
An online medical certificate is not the right choice for emergencies, for anyone under 16 or for any uses the service excludes. The doctor may also decline any request.
Chest pain, trouble breathing, heavy bleeding or a serious injury need emergency care or an in person visit straight away, not a chat. DrCertificate is for suitable non emergency situations only.
Certificates from DrCertificate are not for submission in India and not for legal purposes. The certificates must not be used for insurance.
Recovery and caretaker certificates are not offered, so leave to care for a family member needs another route.
If your illness lasts longer than an online note can cover, see a doctor in person.
Medical certificate for leave in Singapore, Malaysia and the rest of South East Asia

DrCertificate serves people in 10 South East Asian countries. Singapore, Malaysia and Brunei are on the list, as are the Philippines and Indonesia. Thailand and Vietnam are included, along with Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar.

Sick leave and fitness rules differ by country and by employer. Each country sets its own leave entitlement in labour law, and employers add their own rules on top. Your contract or student handbook usually says when a note is needed and who may issue it.

For the official position, go to your national labour ministry. In Singapore that is the Ministry of Manpower, in the Philippines the Department of Labor and Employment, and in Malaysia the Department of Labour.
Then confirm with your employer, school or airline that an online note works for them.
The country guides cover local details.

blocks.text: What does a medical certificate online cost and how long does it take?

A medical certificate online from DrCertificate costs 25 SGD in Singapore, 399 pesos in the Philippines and 30 MYR in Malaysia. Prices in the other served countries depend on where you are and show on the form.
The fee covers the doctor's review of your request in a digital chat and, if approved, the certificate sent by email as a PDF. A decision usually takes about 30 minutes.
Payments are non refundable, including when the doctor declines. The only exception is a verified technical fault within 24 hours.

Frequently asked questions about getting a medical certificate online for leave
Can a medical certificate online be backdated?

DrCertificate does not promise backdated certificates. The doctor sets the dates on each certificate based on what you share in the chat, and may decline dates that do not fit your symptoms. Apply as soon as you feel unwell, and ask whether your employer accepts notes covering days before the consultation.
How long can an online sick leave certificate cover?

The doctor decides how long a sick leave certificate covers, case by case. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms. If you need longer, or your symptoms keep getting worse, see a doctor in person instead.
Do I have to talk to the doctor?

Yes, but only by digital chat. After you submit the form and pay, an independent doctor reviews your request and may message you with follow-up questions. DrCertificate has no video or in person consultations, so reply in the chat promptly to keep your request moving.
What happens if the doctor declines my request?

If the doctor declines, no certificate is issued and the payment is not refunded. Doctors decline about 2% of requests, usually because the name and ID do not match or the symptoms and details are inconsistent. Fill in the form carefully and accurately to avoid this outcome.
Can I get a medical certificate for work from home?

Yes. Choose the Work From Home option on the DrCertificate form if you feel able to work but should stay away from the office. A doctor reviews your request in a chat and decides whether a work from home certificate suits your situation and for how long.
Can I fix a mistake on my certificate after it is issued?

No, unless the error came from the medical team. A certificate cannot be corrected once issued in any other case. Check your name, ID details and dates on the form before you pay, because mistakes you make on the form stay on the certificate.
Is an online medical certificate valid in the Philippines?

An online medical certificate can be used in the Philippines when your employer or school accepts online notes. A doctor registered with a medical council issues it after a chat review. Acceptance is the organisation's decision, so confirm with HR or your school office before you apply.
